newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA CRUMBLE AGAINST INDIAN SPIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA CRUMBLE AGAINST INDIAN SPIN.

text.p: Australia crumbled from 81 for one to 182 all out against India's spinners on a dry and cracked pitch on the first day of the one-off test on Thursday.
Leg-spinner Anil Kumble snapped up four for 63, left-arm spinner Sunil Joshi captured two for 36 and Aashish Kapoor took two for 30 with his off-breaks.
Paceman Venkatesh Prasad and a run out accounted for the other two wickets after Australia won the toss on a surface that was expected to aid the slow bowlers.
Prasad made the initial breakthrough, trapping captain Mark Taylor lbw for 27, and Ricky Ponting was yorked by Kapoor for 14 in the last over before lunch.
Ponting's dismissal marked the start of a decline in which Australia's last nine wickets tumbled for 101.

Top scorer Michael Slater was caught and bowled by Kumble for 44, made in 130 minutes off 96 deliveries and including six fours, and Steve Waugh (0) was caught behind by a fumbling Nayan Mongia off an inside edge off Kapoor.
Mark Waugh and Michael Bevan briefly checked the slide by adding 49 for the fifth wicket before Bevan, playing across the line, was trapped leg before by Joshi for 26.
Waugh also made 26 before falling to Joshi, and Kumble then polished off the lower order, the last six wickets crashing for 39.
